undo-subtraction.name: Undo subtraction
undo-subtraction.when: A number is subtracted from x.
steps: Add that number to both sides.
Simplify to leave x.

undo-addition.name: Undo addition
undo-addition.when: A number is added to x.
steps: Subtract that number from both sides.
Simplify to leave x.

undo-multiplication.name: Undo multiplication
steps: Divide both sides by the coefficient.
Simplify to find one x.

undo-division.name: Undo division
undo-division.when: x is divided by a number.
steps: Multiply both sides by that number.
Simplify to leave x.

reversed.name: Read an equation with x on the right
reversed.when: The unknown is on the right of the equals sign.
steps: Either keep the equation in this order or swap the two complete sides.
Use the same inverse operation on both sides.

two-step.name: Undo two operations
two-step.when: An x-term has an added or subtracted constant.
steps: Undo the addition or subtraction on both sides.
Undo multiplication by dividing both sides.

collect.name: Collect like terms first
collect.when: More than one x-term occurs on the same side.
steps: Combine their coefficients, keeping x.
Undo the constant, then the remaining coefficient.

two-step-division.name: Undo an added constant and division
two-step-division.when: An expression such as x ÷ a + b equals a number.
steps: Undo the added or subtracted constant first.
Multiply both sides by the divisor.

factor.name: Divide out a common factor
factor.when: Every term on both sides has a common factor.
steps: Identify a factor of every term.
Divide every term on both sides by that factor.
Solve the simpler equation.

expand.name: Expand brackets before balancing
expand.when: Expanding a bracket will expose the terms that must be gathered.
steps: Multiply every bracket term by the outside coefficient, retaining signs.
Collect x-terms on one side, then undo the constant and coefficient.

both-sides.name: Gather x-terms from both sides
steps: Subtract the same x-term from both sides.
Undo the constant on the x side.
Divide both sides by the remaining coefficient.

divide-bracket.name: Divide before expanding
divide-bracket.when: A whole bracket is multiplied by a number and the other side divides easily by it.
steps: Divide both whole sides by the outside multiplier.
Solve the equation inside the bracket.

start.name: Undo subtraction by adding
start.question: maths:M10-S01-C1-Q1
annotations: We want x on its own. Here, 7 is being subtracted from x.
Add 7 to both sides to undo subtracting 7. The two sides stay equal.
The −7 and +7 cancel, leaving one x. On the right, 5 + 7 = 12.

start.name: Undo addition by subtracting
annotations: Undo the +7 to leave one x.
Subtract 7 from both sides to keep the equation balanced.

start.name: Undo multiplication with x on the right
start.question: maths:M10-S04-C1-Q5
annotations: The right side is seven lots of x.
Swap the two complete sides; they still have equal value.
Divide both sides by 7 to leave one x.

start.name: Undo division by multiplying
start.question: maths:M10-S05-C1-Q4
annotations: x is divided by 2. Multiplication will undo that division.
Multiply both sides by 2.

build.name: Undo addition, then multiplication
build.question: maths:M10-S01-C2-Q1
annotations: First isolate the term 4x, then find the value of one x.
Subtract 3 from both sides to remove the +3 beside 4x.
This leaves 4x = 28: four lots of x have a total of 28.
Divide both sides by 4 because 4x means four times x.
One x remains. Its value is 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

build.name: Factorise and divide both whole sides
annotations: Every term is divisible by 6. A common factor can simplify the equation.
6 is a common factor of both terms on the left: 6x + 12 = 6(x + 2).
Divide both whole sides by 6. This removes the outside multiplier.
Subtract 2 from both sides to leave one x.

build.name: Undo subtraction, then multiplication
build.question: maths:M10-S04-C2-Q1
annotations: First leave the term 6x on its own.
Add 3 to both sides to undo subtracting 3.
57 + 3 = 60, leaving six lots of x.
Divide both sides by 6 to find one x.
60 ÷ 6 = 10. Check in the original equation.

build.name: Collect like terms before solving
build.question: maths:M10-S04-C2-Q5
annotations: There are two x-terms on the left.
5x + x = 6x. The constant 8 stays separate.
Subtract 8 from both sides.
The right side becomes 0.
Divide both sides by 6.
Zero divided by 6 is 0, so x = 0.

build.name: Undo addition, then division
build.question: maths:M10-P3-PL-C2-Q5
annotations: First remove the added 7.
Subtract 7 from both sides.
12 − 7 = 5, leaving x divided by 3.
Multiply both sides by 3 to undo division.

confidence.name: Expand brackets with x on both sides
confidence.question: maths:M10-S01-C3-Q1
annotations: There are x-terms on both sides. Expand first, then gather those terms on one side.
Multiply every term inside the bracket by 3: 3 × x + 3 × 2 = 3x + 6.
Subtract x from both sides. This removes the smaller x-term on the right.
On the left, 3x − x = 2x. The right side is now just 24.
Subtract 6 from both sides to leave the term 2x on its own.
Two lots of x equal 18. We still need the value of one x.
Divide both sides by 2 to change 2x into one x.
One x equals 9. Substitute 9 into the original brackets to check.

confidence.name: Divide the bracket before expanding
annotations: Both sides have a factor of 3. Dividing first is shorter than expanding here.
3 is a common factor, so divide both sides by 3 to simplify.
The bracket becomes x + 4, and 27 ÷ 3 = 9.
Subtract 4 from both sides to leave one x.

confidence.name: Gather x-terms without brackets
confidence.question: maths:M10-S04-C3-Q4
annotations: There are x-terms on both sides.
Subtract x from both sides.
4x − x = 3x; the right side is now 14.
Subtract 2 from both sides.
Divide both sides by 3.
12 ÷ 3 = 4. Check both original sides give 18.

confidence.name: Factorise before solving
confidence.question: maths:M10-S04-C3-Q2
annotations: Both left-hand terms have a factor of 5.
Write 5x + 10 as 5(x + 2).
Divide both whole sides by 5.
Subtract 2 from both sides.

confidence.name: Expand a bracket containing subtraction
confidence.question: maths:M10-S04-C3-Q1
annotations: Distribute the 3 to both terms inside the bracket.
Subtract 2x from both sides.
Add 9 to both sides.
−11 + 9 = −2. Check in the original bracket.
